summary: Ram Chandra Kak was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied at Sri Pratap College and trained under John Marshall. He served as curator of Sri Pratap Singh Museum, Archaeological Survey of India superintendent, and Kashmir's Director of Archæology and Research.

Indologist and linguist Ram Karan Sharma earned an MA from Patna University and a PhD from UC Berkeley under Murray Barnson Emeneau. He was vice chancellor of Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga and Sampurnanand Sanskrit Universities, alongside holding several visiting professorships.

Ram Mohan Roy was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He founded several influential organizations and institutions, including Atmiya Sabha (1814), Presidency College, Kolkata (1816), Anglo-Hindu School (1822), Vedanta College (1826), and the Brahmo Samaj (1828).

Ram Niwas Pandey is an archaeologist and Indologist. He pursued his education at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University and the Institute of Archaeology, completing his doctoral studies under the supervision of Hit Narayan Jha.

Ram Shankar Tripathi specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He served as Head of Bauddhadarśana at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Dean of Śabdavidyā at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and visiting faculty at Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Historian and Indologist Ram Sharan Sharma studied at Patna University and earned a PhD from SOAS under A. L. Basham. He headed history departments at Patna University and Delhi University, and was founding president of the Indian Council of Historical Research.
Rama Misra Shastri was an Indologist and philosopher. He held the post of assistant Professor of Sáṅkhya at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, attested in both 1882 and 1914.

Linguist and Indologist Rama Nath Sharma studied at BHU, Allahabad, Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University, and the University of Rochester (PhD). He taught at the University of Allahabad before holding professorships at the University of Rochester and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.

Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Martin Haug, at Elphinstone College, Mumbai University, and Göttingen (PhD). He served as professor at Elphinstone and Deccan Colleges, and as Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai.

Ramaprasad Chanda worked in Indology and archaeology, studying at Scottish Church College and Dhaka College. He served as Superintendent of the Indian Museum's Archaeological Section (1921–1932) and president of the Indian Anthropological Institute (1938–1942), which he also founded.

Indologist Ramaranjan Mukherji held degrees from the University of Calcutta and Jadavpur University. He served as Head of Sanskrit at Jadavpur University, vice chancellor at the University of Burdwan and Rabindra Bharati University, and chancellor of the National Sanskrit University.
Ramchandra B. Athavale was an Indology scholar who served as Professor of Sanskrit at S.L.D. Arts College (attested in 1938) and as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat Vidyapith.

Indologist Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar earned degrees from Mumbai University and Heidelberg University. He served as professor and Dean of Arts at Savitribai Phule Pune University and was the longtime Honorary Secretary of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute from 1939 to 2001.

Historian and Indologist Ramesh Chandra Majumdar studied at Presidency College and the University of Calcutta. He served as professor, provost, and vice chancellor at the University of Dhaka, principal at BHU and RTM Nagpur University, and president of the Asiatic Society.

Ramesh Shankar Gupte worked in Indology and archaeology. In 1967, he was attested as Head of History & Ancient Indian Culture at Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University and as a visiting lecturer at Wake Forest, Salem College, and Winston-Salem State.

Ramin Etesami is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Geshe Lobsang Jamspal and Krishna Ghosh Della Santina, attested in 2015.
Ramon Prats is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was affiliated with Himalayan and Inner Asian Resources in 1999 and Pompeu Fabra University in 2017.

Randall Studstill is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He was educated under the instruction of Irene Woodward and Steven D. Goodman, and completed doctoral research under the supervision of Richard Payne.

Linguist, sinologist, and tibetologist Randy J. LaPolla earned his doctorate at UC Berkeley under James A. Matisoff. He served as a professor at the City University of Hong Kong (c. 1996–2004) and joined Beijing Normal University, Zhuhai in 2021.

Rangama Chandawimala is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Kakkapalliye Anuruddha Thera. He was attested as Associate Professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.
